rows.evidence: Q1: Materials and methods <U+2013> three-season field trial (1997<U+2013>1999) at Tel Amara, Bekaa, with 15N microplots, tensiometers, neutron probe and tensionics soil-solution extractors at 30, 60 and 80 cm. Q2: Nitrate leaching evaluation section and Figure 6 <U+2013> across the season significantly higher nitrate concentrations were found under the macro-sprinkler below the roots (60 and 80 cm), whereas both fertigation and drip treatments showed a steady, very low nitrate level at 80 cm; regardless of fertilizer method, trickle irrigation showed no risk of vertical nitrate movement; estimated N leached below the root zone under 3 kg/ha for drip versus 55 kg/ha for sprinkler; Conclusions restate that drip treatments showed steady low nitrates beyond the root zone. Q4: Fertilizer use efficiency section <U+2013> soil head potential at 30 cm under sprinklers varied between -175 and -100 mbar so the profile was wet to the full width of the beds (one-dimensional flow pattern), neutron-probe water use showed sprinkler roots took relatively more water (39%) from the 30<U+2013>60 cm layer and tensiometers at 60 cm showed weak fluctuation (-100 to -50 mbar), indicating deeper water penetration, in contrast to localized drip wetting.
rows.notes: Leaching comparison rests on one method (tensionics soil-solution nitrate concentrations); the kg/ha leached estimate combines those concentrations with literature-derived irrigation efficiencies rather than an independent measurement, so Q3 is no. Single site, soil (clay Typic Xerorthent), crop (potato cv Spunta) and plot scale (largest plots 1250 m2 on-station). No conditions stated as requirements for the reduced-leaching effect and no limitations stated for the leaching result (the sampling-variability caveat concerns yield). Figure 6 significance is reported only via statistical difference; no dispersion measure for leaching values. Comparison is drip/fertigation vs macro-sprinkler, not flood irrigation.

notes: Full text appears complete. Figures are referenced but not reproduced, so presence of error bars on Figure 6 could not be verified; Figure 3 (shoot dry matter) is stated to show standard errors but that is not the leaching result.
